leads.title: Criminal Law Amendment Act, 1968-69 (Bill C-150)
leads.documents: Federal decriminalization of same-sex sexual activity in private between consenting adults, applicable in British Columbia; foundation for legal status.
leads.detail: Cited as brought into force upon royal assent on June 27, 1969; introduced in 1967 by then-Justice Minister Pierre Trudeau with quote 'There's no place for the state in the bedrooms of the nation.' No URL visible.

leads.title: Canadian Charter of Rights and Freedoms - Section 15(1), Section 1, Section 33
leads.documents: Constitutional equality machinery enforceable against all laws and government institutions including law enforcement in BC; reasonable limits (Oakes Test) and notwithstanding clause framework.
leads.detail: Quotes s.15(1) text on equality without discrimination; notes Charter in Constitution 1982, in force 1985; s.1 reasonable limits, s.33 five-year exemption, s.2 religion, s.93 denominational schools. No URL visible.

leads.title: Egan v. Canada (1995) - Supreme Court of Canada
leads.documents: Landmark ruling that sexual orientation is constitutionally protected under s.15 Charter as analogous ground; binds BC courts and legislatures.
leads.detail: Cited as 1995 landmark decision; reaffirmed 2008 quote on promotion of equality. No URL visible.

leads.title: Vriend v Alberta (1998) - Supreme Court of Canada
leads.documents: Held failure of provincial legislature to include sexual orientation in human rights law itself violates s.15; precedent for BC provincial human rights obligations.
leads.detail: Cited as 1998 decision; context for statement that as of 2017 all provinces, territories and federal government explicitly include sexual orientation and gender identity in human rights acts. No URL visible.

leads.title: Civil Marriage Act (Federal, July 20, 2005) and Supreme Court Reference (December 2004)
leads.documents: Nationwide legalization of same-sex marriage including BC; confirms federal jurisdiction over capacity to marry.
leads.detail: Parliament passed bill July 20, 2005 making Canada 4th country nationwide; Supreme Court declared proposed definition consistent with Charter and within exclusive Parliament authority; Ontario Court of Appeal immediate effect followed by other provinces. No URL visible.

leads.title: Criminal Code Section 159 and repeal via Bill C-32 / Bill C-75
leads.documents: Former anal intercourse offence with unequal age rules; BC enforcement history relevant to visitor safety dossier.
leads.detail: s.159 criminalized anal intercourse if under 18 or >2 persons present; courts in Ontario, Quebec, British Columbia, Nova Scotia, Alberta each declared s.159 unconstitutional; Bill C-32 then C-75 tabled March 2018, royal assent June 21, 2019 setting age 16; statement by MP Randy Boissonnault special advisor on LGBTQ2 issues. No URL visible.

leads.title: Expungement of Historically Unjust Convictions Act (2018) - Parole Board of Canada
leads.documents: Federal redress machinery for pre-1969 homosexual acts and s.159 convictions; directs RCMP and federal departments to destroy/remove records and notify provincial/municipal police and courts including BC.
leads.detail: Royal assent June 21, 2018 by Governor General; PM Justin Trudeau apology Nov 28, 2017 quoted; Parole Board states expungement different from pardon/record suspension, available to living and deceased. No URL visible.

leads.title: Canadian Human Rights Act and Provincial Human Rights Laws - BC application
leads.documents: Anti-discrimination and anti-harassment protections in employment, housing, public/private accommodations in BC on sexual orientation and gender identity or expression; vital statistics gender-change rules.
leads.detail: Cited that discrimination prohibited by all provinces/territories and federal government; Canadian Human Rights Act limited to federal workplaces (banks, aviation, inter-provincial transport) while provincial laws cover most schools, rental housing, health care, workplaces; transgender legal gender change allowed in all provinces/territories under varying rules. No URL visible.

leads.title: Federal Court Challenges Program (expanded 1985)
leads.documents: Federal funding mechanism that funded s.15 Charter test cases advancing LGBTQ rights enforceable in BC.
leads.detail: Cited as expanded in 1985 to fund test cases challenging federal legislation on Charter equality rights; provincial challenge funding varied by province. No URL visible.

leads.title: Canadian Association of Chiefs of Police Apology (December 2020) - Equity, Diversity and Inclusion Committee
leads.documents: Institutional policing acknowledgment of decades of oppression of Two-Spirit, Lesbian, Gay, Bisexual, Transgender, Queer communities and commitment to non-discrimination, relevant to enforcement experience in BC.
leads.detail: Issued on International Day of Human Rights Dec 2020; quotes apology for institutional bias and violation of human rights; creation of Equity, Diversity and Inclusion Committee to mitigate implicit bias. No URL visible.
